# Rule 2.3 - Metafriending / Metagrudging
"Metafriending" refers to favoring a particular player's character (a "metafriend") when your character should have no in-character reason to do so, such as giving out special items or access to that particular player's character. Maintaining a friendship over multiple rounds is perfectly acceptable, but don't give overly special treatment just because of the past.
"Metagrudging" refers to hating or otherwise acting negatively in-game towards a particular player's character when your character should have no in-character reason to be acting hostile towards them. Don't do this. Be civil and resolve any out-of-character issues up front.
Characters are allowed to have persistent relationships/friendships/rivalries across rounds; however, in-character relationships should not be used to gain an unfair advantage, and it shouldn't devolve into metagrudging either.
Additionally, do not play a character to only interact with a specific person or people, then ignore everyone else.
## Precedents - Character friendships should not be used to gain an unfair advantage. Having an in-character friendship with another player does not, for example, justify giving them all-access each round. - Character rivalries don't justify metagrudging or [textlink="self-antagging" link="RuleSelfantag"]. - Character relationships do not justify cross-teaming, such as helping out a [textlink="Changeling" link="Changelings"].
